data_domains: global news monitoring; article-level metadata; tone and theme coding; television and image indexes
notes: Filter Libya with sourcecountry:LY or by language. The DOC API refuses more than one request every 5 seconds and says so in the response body rather than with a 429, so a naive loop silently collects error text. Bulk history is in BigQuery.

data_domains: aggregator: administrative boundaries; population; displacement; health and education facilities; damage assessments; security incidents
notes: CKAN API, fq=groups:lby. Top providers for Libya: World Bank 23, UNOSAT 22, HOT 12, OCHA ROMENA 11, Insecurity Insight 10, REACH 8, WorldPop 7. Already used in this repository for COD-AB boundaries. Licences vary per dataset and several are share-alike or non-commercial.

data_domains: satellite damage assessment; flood extent; building damage; displacement site mapping
notes: Analyst-verified imagery products, so the interpretation is already done. Derna flood 2023 and successive conflict damage assessments are the largest Libya holdings. Reached through HDX rather than the UNOSAT site.

data_domains: refugees; asylum seekers; IDPs; returned refugees and IDPs; stateless persons, by origin and asylum country
notes: Open API, no key. Query coo=LBY for Libyans displaced and coa=LBY for people displaced into Libya. Returned 278,177 IDPs in Libya for 2020 in the probe.

data_domains: IDP and returnee baseline assessments by mahalla and baladiya; migrant stock and nationality; flow monitoring
notes: The single best subnational source on Libya after the census, and it is keyed to the same baladiya and mahalla names this repository already harmonises. dtm.iom.int/api returned 403 and dtmapi.iom.int returned 404 on every path tried; reach it through the four HDX datasets instead.

producer: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data
data_domains: geocoded political violence and protest events; actors; fatalities; event type and sub-event type
notes: The reference conflict event dataset for Libya. Unauthenticated reads now return {"message":"Access denied"} and /oauth/token answers 405 to GET, so the free-key OAuth flow is mandatory. Actor names are the natural join to an armed-group roster.

data_domains: georeferenced event dataset; battle deaths; one-sided and non-state violence
notes: Libya is country 620. The API now answers 'API token required. Add header: x-ucdp-access-token'. Annual releases are also downloadable as flat files. Narrower than ACLED but with a longer and more conservative coding history.

producer: UN Security Council Libya Sanctions Committee (1970)
data_domains: designated individuals and entities; Panel of Experts annual reports; asset freeze and travel ban records
notes: The consolidated list is a single 2.1 MB XML; Libya designations carry reference numbers LYi.001 upward and LYe.001 upward. The Panel of Experts reports are the richer OSINT product: named procurement chains, oil smuggling networks and armed-group finances, published as PDFs on the committee page.

producer: US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control
data_domains: Specially Designated Nationals; blocked entities; sanctions programme tags
notes: Filter on the LIBYA2 and LIBYA3 programme tags. Complements the UN list, since US designations are broader and sometimes earlier.

data_domains: merged sanctions lists; politically exposed persons; company and officer records, entity-resolved across sources
notes: The PEPs collection holds 710,657 targets and ships as a 178 MB CSV or a 1.3 GB nested JSON; the sanctions collection holds 293,095 entities. The search API needs a key but the bulk files do not. This is the fastest route to a Libyan PEP roster, and it carries the UN and OFAC Libya designations already resolved.

data_domains: officeholders and terms of office; institutions; settlements; administrative units; identifiers linking to other databases
notes: SPARQL returns 151 people holding a position applicable to Libya, 135 of those statements carrying a start date. Small and uneven, but CC0 and already linked to VIAF and national identifiers, so it is a seed and a reconciliation target rather than a source of record.

producer: Internet Outage Detection and Analysis, Georgia Tech
data_domains: country and ASN level internet connectivity; outage alerts from BGP, active probing and darknet telescope
notes: Shutdowns and connectivity collapses are a direct observable of conflict and of state behaviour. Query entityType=country&entityCode=LY.

data_domains: censorship measurements; blocked websites and apps; per-network test results from volunteer probes
notes: Measures which sites are blocked on which Libyan networks. Volunteer-collected, so coverage is thin and irregular; treat absence as absence of measurement.

data_domains: ADS-B aircraft state vectors; historical flight tracks
notes: Anonymous access works with a bounding box and returns live state vectors; historical queries need a free account. Coverage over Libya depends on volunteer receivers and is sparse inland.

data_domains: unfiltered ADS-B including military and state aircraft
notes: The unfiltered feed is what makes it useful for Libya: aircraft other trackers suppress are visible. The map is free, the API is commercial.

data_domains: arbitrary OSM feature queries; settlements; roads; facilities; administrative relations
notes: ODbL, so anything derived from it carries share-alike terms; this repository already isolates OSM output under data/external/. Reachable, though count queries timed out at the sizes tried.

data_domains: situation reports; assessments; press releases; job and training postings, tagged by country, theme and organisation
notes: A full-text corpus of humanitarian reporting on Libya going back to 1996, free once an appname is registered. The v2 endpoint rejects unregistered appnames and v1 returned 410 on the call tried.

data_domains: civilian harm allegations from airstrikes and shelling; per-incident sourcing and casualty estimates
notes: Incident-level records with explicit source chains and confidence grading, covering the 2011 intervention and later strikes. Published as structured pages rather than an API.

data_domains: open-source investigations; geolocated imagery; equipment and actor identification
notes: Method and case material rather than a dataset. Their Libya work on mercenary deployments and strike attribution is the closest thing to documented geolocation practice for the country.

data_domains: mission statements; ceasefire and political process documents; human rights reporting with OHCHR
notes: Primary record of the internationally mediated political process, and the naming authority for many of the bodies an officials dataset would need.

data_domains: English-language Libyan business, energy and political reporting
notes: RSS works; no sitemap index at the standard path. The longest-running English outlet on Libya and the most consistent on oil and banking.

data_domains: English and Arabic Libyan political reporting, Tripoli-aligned editorial line
notes: No RSS or sitemap at the standard paths, so enumeration needs link crawling. Pair with an eastern-aligned outlet to avoid a one-sided corpus.

data_domains: English-language Libyan news
notes: WordPress REST API open, 6,160 posts, the same enumeration pattern already used for HNEC and parliament.ly. The cheapest full-text Libyan news corpus to build.

data_domains: Arabic Libyan news, independent editorial line
notes: Returns 403 to this address, the same pattern as the seven Libyan hosts recorded in access_notes.md. Loads normally from an ordinary connection.

data_domains: monthly oil production, refining, stocks, imports and exports as reported by member countries
notes: Self-reported, and Libyan submissions are incomplete across the conflict years, which is itself informative. Cross-check against OPEC secondary sources and tanker tracking.

data_domains: VIIRS and MODIS active fire and thermal anomaly detections
notes: Thermal anomalies over Libyan oil infrastructure are a flaring and throughput proxy at daily resolution, and a conflict indicator elsewhere. Country code LBY. Needs a free MAP_KEY; DEMO_KEY is rejected.

data_domains: leaked and scraped document collections; company registries; entity search across investigations
notes: Holds several Libya-relevant collections including procurement and offshore material. Access tiers differ per collection and some need journalist credentials.

data_domains: company registrations and officers across jurisdictions
notes: Libya has no open company register, so coverage of Libyan-domiciled firms is close to nil. Useful in the other direction: foreign firms with Libyan contracts, which joins to the CBL letter-of-credit beneficiary data already in this repository.

data_domains: AIS vessel tracks; port visits; loitering and encounter events
notes: AIS is the open route to Libyan oil export and smuggling monitoring: tanker port calls at Es Sider, Ras Lanuf, Zawiya and Brega, and ship-to-ship transfers offshore. Commercial trackers cover this better but cost money.

data_domains: traffic volume by country and ASN; outage annotations; protocol and device mix
notes: A second, independent read on Libyan connectivity alongside IODA, useful because the two disagree on some events.

data_domains: international petroleum production, consumption, trade and reserves
notes: Independent estimates of Libyan crude production, which is the series NOC and OPEC report differently.

data_domains: documentation of enforced disappearance, detention and killings
notes: The domain now serves a FingerprintJS script that redirects with a tracking UUID, not the organisation's site. Treat anything collected from it after this date as untrusted and source their documentation from mirrors or from their social accounts instead.
